required_prompts.text: What did we discover that was not explicit before, and what exact evidence made it visible?
What could disprove the finding, and what conflicting or missing evidence have we considered?
Which declared dependencies, actors, decisions or sources connect apparently separate candidate routes?
Which verification question or review could most change our available options?
Are we still working towards the client’s explicit target and success criteria?
What may be stale, what could follow from our actions, and what event should make us reconsider?
Which findings belong in 8BALL, ENDSTATE, an existing task, or a retained future candidate?
What are we not implementing, why, and where can the owner review or reopen that choice?
What actually passed, what failed, and which claimed capabilities still need independent or native verification?
What might we still have missed, and how can the operator or owner record their own hypothesis?
What course has an authorised human selected, and what exactly would require reconsideration rather than an automatic switch?
Which available inputs were not processed, what limits bound this conclusion, and what could exist outside the current catalogue?
When analysis fails, what safe recovery is available, who contributed the correction, and is the original failure still recorded?
Can the exact implementation and evidence for every delivery claim be recovered, or must that claim remain reported-only?
Does this improve the operator’s next decision or merely increase reviews, alerts and screens? How would we measure the difference?

items.title: Signed local audit bytes do not establish independent checkpoint custody
items.origin: operations-2101512c
items.observation: Signing/verifying real Ed25519 checkpoints rejects altered digest, scope, revision and key, but the tool cannot verify that key or checkpoint custody is independent of the database administrator.
items.product_implication: Production audit claims require separately trusted key/checkpoint custody, rotation and external anchoring rather than an extra local hash.

history.reason: existing_task: keep the signed engineering seam in B03-05 and preserve independent custody/production acceptance as explicit external gates.

items.title: Current revocation observations are not remote revocation commands or atomicity
items.origin: operations-2101512c
items.observation: Transactional tests show missing/unavailable surface probes cannot establish denial, close must rerun all six surfaces, and adapter failure or post-command revocation rolls back. A local transaction cannot guarantee atomic remote vault/search/worker state.
items.product_implication: Use fresh scoped probes and current authority, distinguish unavailable from denied, and require host-reviewed remote consistency rather than declaring a local journal entry globally revoked.

history.reason: existing_task: retain fail-closed observations in B03-05 with explicit injection/remote-service gates; no cross-lane revocation command is invented.

items.title: Confidential support metadata needs a separately controlled diagnostic narrative
items.origin: operations-2101512c
items.observation: Strict operation schemas and sanitized probe-exception tests exclude arbitrary source text and adapter exception details while preserving opaque IDs, category, revision and evidence digests. That exclusion alone does not show that an incident can be diagnosed adequately.
items.product_implication: Keep detailed support reports in separately authorised evidence storage and measure triage/correction burden with authorised operators; do not restore sensitive free text to operational logs for convenience.

history.reason: existing_task: keep constrained metadata and document controlled support evidence handling. Diagnostic sufficiency remains an operator-evaluation hypothesis, not a new required product.

items.title: A clean scan verdict is publishable only for its exact live attempt and vault revision
items.observation: Revocation, scan cancellation and hold/retention revision changes during scanning invalidate publication even when a scanner later reports clean. Interrupted scans must not automatically resume or repeat on command replay.
items.product_implication: Keep scan claim, processing and release separate; recheck current authority and exact attempt/revision at publication, require explicit cancellation/restart and state that cancellation cannot recall bytes already supplied to a scanner.

items.title: Local ciphertext deletion is not proof of storage-wide or legal erasure
items.observation: Deleting a local encrypted blob can preserve an immutable descriptor and audited tombstone while leaving derived text, WAL/filesystem remnants, backups, replicas and provider retention outside its scope. Without current dependency clearance the vault must deny deletion.
items.product_implication: Label deletion local_vault_ciphertext_only, enforce hold/retention plus same-transaction dependency guard and preserve independent erasure/recovery evidence as an existing B03-02 production gate.
items.origin: Vault builder 2026-10-25 / session9c76974dc65748658ac94e333ea877fd

items.title: Reviewed source handles are references, not future publication authority
items.observation: A source handle returned before projection publication can become stale, revoked or unavailable. The final source gate must run on the caller's same-database transaction and verify current scope, exact revision/hash, clean release and authenticated ciphertext, with audit rolled back alongside the mutation.
items.product_implication: Use Vault.require_source(db, identity=..., case_id=..., object_id=..., expected_revision=..., expected_sha256=...) immediately at final shared BEGIN IMMEDIATE commit/publish boundary; never authorize from a cached handle or separate connection.
items.origin: Vault builder 2026-10-25 / session9c76974dc65748658ac94e333ea877fd

history.reason: existing_task: added safe metadata-only transaction gate and rollback/staleness/revocation/quarantine/ciphertext tests for B03-02 integration; collaboration wrapper agreement and cumulative integration tests remain separate.

items.title: Content-envelope encryption and a local audit chain do not solve metadata custody
items.observation: AES-GCM protects original bytes and authenticates their descriptor, but filenames, scope metadata and audit identifiers remain outside the content envelope. SQLite triggers/hash chains do not protect against an administrator rewriting or truncating the database and chain.
items.product_implication: Require explicit whole-storage protection, key custody, independent audit anchoring and recovery threat review before any production claim; do not relabel the local wrapper/audit chain as managed infrastructure.
items.origin: Vault builder 2026-10-25 / session9c76974dc65748658ac94e333ea877fd

items.title: A fictional fixture authorisation and token ceiling do not establish an enforced spend cap
items.origin: Anthropic failed-run preflight review / 2026-10-26
items.observation: Four Sonnet 4.6 requests were attempted before the repository-required provider-enforced US$5 cap and disabled automatic top-up were confirmed. All returned HTTP400; safe retained diagnostics omit the precise cause. A later model-catalogue HTTP200 does not establish credits, billing limits or successful inference. The omission was disclosed and further inference stopped.
items.product_implication: Make billing preflight a separate explicit gate from credentials and model selection. Preserve failed receipts without attributing an unknown error to newer model rules. No automatic retry or budget increase; a future enforceable application spend ledger remains separate engineering.
